title: MCP check registry entry
description: One listed MCP server: servers/<owner>/<repo>.json, or servers/<owner>/<repo>~<path-slug>.json for a folder listing ("~" can't occur in a GitHub repository name; the listing page uses the same <repo>~<path-slug>), where path-slug is the folder path lower-cased with every character outside [a-z0-9] turned into '-'. Everything is lower-case.

id.description: Lower-case owner/repo, for a folder listing too (the folder is in path). The claim file names this.

path.description: Subfolder of the server inside the repository; empty for the root.

defaultBranch.description: The repository's default branch, from the GitHub API, as GitHub spells it. Used for the one-click Add-to-CI and claim links.

by.description: GitHub login of the person who submitted it.

issue.description: Submission issue number in this repository; null for entries added directly.

commit.description: Commit of the default branch (or of the listed subfolder's branch) that was read.

source.description: How the tool definitions were found. repo-static: read from the source; nothing was run.

status.description: ok: graded. no-tools: the static reader found no tool definitions.

error.description: Why the scan did not grade, when status is not ok: the checker's message on one line, without control characters.

fidelity.description: exact (a committed list or snapshots), literal (literal definitions in the source), derived (reproduced from SDK registrations) or names (names only).

surface.description: Always null since rubric 2.2.0 (mcp-check 1.2.0): the write surface is reported as guard coverage, not a letter. Earlier scans: null when there was no write surface to grade.

findings.description: Counts by severity. high = the checker's blocking items, medium = attention, low = advice.

verified.description: A workflow file on the default branch uses isokron-ai/mcp-check.

workflow.description: Path of the first workflow that uses it, or empty.

verified.description: The default branch holds .github/mcp-check/registry.json: {"id": "<owner/repo>"}, plus "path": "<folder>" for a folder listing.
